title: Medieval Climate Anomaly
summary: The Medieval Climate Anomaly is the name for a warm interval dated by the IPCC to 950 to 1250. Continental-scale reconstructions show multi-decade periods that in some regions were as warm as the mid-20th century and in others as warm as the late 20th century. The warm intervals were less synchronous across seasons and regions than modern warming, and proxy records are heterogeneous.

uncertainty.note: The IPCC and Penn State give 950-1250; PAGES gives a general frame of about 950-1300. The anomaly was not simultaneous across regions.

where.modern_name: Global (no single site; map anchor in the North Atlantic)

importance.justification: Climate interval used as the reference warm period for the last millennium; regional, not synchronous.

beats.caption: Reconstructions show multi-decade warm periods in some regions during the Medieval Climate Anomaly, from 950 to 1250.
Peak warmth was not simultaneous: the warm intervals were less synchronous across seasons and regions than modern warming.
Proxy records and reconstructions differ widely, so researchers still ask where and when it was warm.

reviewer_note: Least sure: no location. The point is a North Atlantic map anchor only, with 20000 km uncertainty, and the pages opened do not name a region; geometry is global. The span has two published endings (1250 and 1300). The IPCC chapter was read from its PDF text (pdftotext). PAGES text had mojibake in "C.E." so spotcheck should use the digits.
